$comment: Conditional branches (`then`, and a `not` inside one) that require a property also declare it as `"properties": { "<name>": true }`. That is deliberately not a constraint - a boolean `true` schema permits anything. It exists because the validator runs Ajv with `strict: true`, and Ajv's `strictRequired` rule rejects a `required` entry whose property is not declared in that same subschema object. Keeping the branch self-contained satisfies the rule without changing its meaning; the valid and invalid fixtures in packages/spec/test cover both directions.
title: AID Framework spec v0.6
description: The declarative source of truth for an AID application. Hand-authored against design doc Â§6, narrowed to the implemented surface (Â§14): the Phase 0 sections (models, prompts, tools, evals, pipelines) plus Phase 1 retrieval (stores, retrievers, the retrieve step and the retrieval metric). Top-level keys outside this set are rejected rather than ignored, so a feature that has not been implemented cannot be silently dropped. Within an implemented section, a sub-feature Phase 1 does not serve is rejected by a spec-local rule (`spec/not-supported`) rather than by the schema, so the enum stays the design doc's and the message can name the phase. See packages/spec/README.md for the scope boundary and the deferred keys.

specVersion.description: Spec language version. Each version's additions are listed in the spec version changelog (`docs/reference/spec-changelog.md`). A section or construct that needs a later version is reported as `spec/not-supported` with the version it needs, rather than as an unknown key.

profile.description: The operating profile: a named bundle of defaults and required controls, not a mode. `standard` is the default and is what an absent `profile` means, so every spec written before 0.25 keeps exactly the behaviour it had. `enterprise` requires the controls a regulated deployment cannot go without, and the profile gate refuses a spec that declares it and then omits them: a region pin on every deployment, an audit sink on every deployment, and at least one guardrail that runs on output. A requirement that a spec could not satisfy is never added to a profile, so `enterprise` is always passable. Declarable from spec v0.25.

types.description: Named structured types referenced by prompts (structured output) and tools (input/output).

models.description: Model aliases. The alias is what the rest of the spec refers to; the vendor id is pinned here and only here.

stores.description: Vector store instances. `kind: memory` is the fully supported default and needs no service; `kind: pgvector` is declarable here and its adapter ships with the retrieval runtime.

retrievers.description: Retrievers: what to index, how to chunk it, which embedding model and store to use, and how to rank.

knowledgeBases.description: Managed knowledge bases: a source, chunker, embedding pass, store and index the cloud owns, referenced by a retriever's `knowledgeBase`. Declarable from spec v0.12. A managed knowledge base is a retriever, not a pipeline: the runtime still retrieves chunks and generates the answer, so the cost gate, the evals and the trace keep covering the generation path.

gateways.description: Managed MCP gateways: an endpoint the cloud hosts, fronting federated tool targets, reached by a runtime over MCP instead of bundling every tool into it. Declarable from spec v0.24, and AWS only: the resource is Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway. A gateway federates tools the spec does not own -- this is not a second generation path for `tools:`, which keeps emitting the same local tool registry whether or not a gateway exists. Every target kind lives under the gateway's one `Mcp` target union, which is why a target is one shape with a `kind` discriminator rather than sibling keys: the CloudFormation resource accepts no top-level OpenAPI target. The `authorizer` is required because a gateway with no authentication is reachable by anyone who learns its URL, and neither `NONE` nor `AUTHENTICATE_ONLY` is reachable from this surface.

agents.description: Agents: a model, instructions, the tools and retrievers it may use, and the budget it may spend. Declarable from spec v0.2; a target that emits no agent route is rejected by the capability gate rather than silently generating one.

guardrails.description: Guardrails: the stages a check runs at, the policies it evaluates, and what happens when one fails. Declarable from spec v0.2. The runtime evaluates them and both targets (`py-fastapi` and `ts-vercel`) emit the wiring; a guardrail declared here applies to every pipeline route of the document, not to the one that named it.

decisions.description: Decision points answered by TypeSafe AI Jev: a named question with its own reply shape, referenced by guardrails, routers and evals. Declarable from spec v0.6. A decision is not a provider, because Jev has no chat surface: it returns a typed answer rather than text. `choice` and `score` require `criteria`; `noul` forbids it. A pinned model version is the reproducible choice; an eval reference refuses a moving alias, while interactive routing may use one.

memory.description: Memory tiers: what is remembered, for how long, within what token budget, and where it lives. Declarable from spec v0.2; the kinds a target cannot serve are refused by its plan gate rather than approximated.

deployments.description: Deployment intents: the target shape, the transport it assumes, and the secrets it needs. Declarable from spec v0.2. `streaming: true` derives a `streaming` requirement; both `py-fastapi` and `ts-vercel` declare that capability and answer an `Accept: text/event-stream` request with SSE frames, and a target that declares nothing is refused by the deploy gate.

name.description: snake_case identifier for a spec node.

typeName.description: UpperCamelCase name of a declared type.

semanticCache.description: Semantic cache settings. `threshold` is the minimum cosine similarity (0..1) a new prompt must reach against a cached one before the cached response is reused; `ttlSeconds` bounds how long a cached response may be reused. Both are required together so a spec cannot opt in with a silent default threshold or TTL.

fieldType.description: A primitive (string, number, integer, boolean) or a declared type name, optionally suffixed with [] for a list.

modelArmorConfidence.description: The lowest confidence at which a Model Armor filter refuses content. The names are the provider's `LOW_AND_ABOVE`, `MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE` and `HIGH`, lowercased into the spec's own vocabulary so a spec never carries a Cloud enum.

namespace.description: Dotted namespace used to qualify generated symbols.

targets.description: Generator targets to emit. Defaults to [py-fastapi] when omitted.

kind.description: Only struct is in spec v0.1. enum/union/list land with the agents work, and adding them is a schema change, not a silent widening.

required.description: Defaults to false. Drives required-vs-optional on the generated side.

enum.$comment: A deliberate, minimal widening beyond the approved Â§3 sketch: structured output is the whole point of spec v0.1 and a classification field is the most common shape it takes. The minimum/maximum keys already establish that scalar constraints belong on a field.

provider.description: The provider set the shipped adapters serve. `fake` is deterministic and keyless, which is what lets the eval gate run offline in CI. `bedrock` takes its credentials from the execution role and `google` (Vertex AI) from a short-lived bearer token supplied by the environment or the metadata server, so neither needs an `apiKeyEnv`. `gemini` is the Gemini API, not Vertex: one API key and no project, location or OAuth2.

modelId.description: Pinned vendor model id. Never an alias or a moving target: the resolved id is recorded in the IR so a run is reproducible.

capabilities.description: Declared model capabilities. json-schema is negotiated within a prompt (a structured-output prompt must bind a model that declares it) and embeddings within a retriever (a retriever's embedModel must declare it); the others are recorded in the IR for the capability gate to use in later phases. The embeddings capability additionally requires a provider that serves an embeddings endpoint: the runtime routes embedding calls by provider (bedrock and google to their own adapters, gemini to the AI Studio adapter, openai and openai-compatible to the OpenAI-compatible wire), so declaring it on anthropic is refused rather than sent over a wire that vendor does not serve.

fallbacks.description: Ordered model aliases to fail over to. Simple alias failover only; no routing policy in Phase 0.

costProfile.description: Name of a priced entry in the pinned model catalog. Omit to resolve it from the catalog by modelId.

baseUrl.description: Required for openai-compatible. Never a credential.

apiKeyEnv.$comment: The *name* of an environment variable, never a key. The pattern cannot express a literal secret, so a committed credential is out of scope by construction.

cache.description: Model caching, declarable from spec v0.3. `prompt` is the exact-match layer (model, prompt, tool schema and temperature); `semantic` is the opt-in fuzzy layer and carries its own threshold and TTL so there is no silent default.

version.description: Bumped by hand when the template changes. The prompt identity includes it (prompt:<name>@<version>) so a revision does not move the IR node id.

template.description: Mustache-style text. Placeholders are {{variable}} references and are checked by the parser for well-formedness; whether each one resolves is a build-time IR gate, not a schema concern.

description.description: Shown to the model once model-selected tool choice exists (Phase 2). Required now so the field never has to be added retroactively.

sideEffects.description: Drives the fail-closed security gate: write and destructive require auth.

requiresConfirmation.description: The agent loop pauses before running this tool and waits for a human decision. A pipeline step has no confirmation step, so a target that emits no agent route refuses the flag rather than ignoring it.

handler.description: Where the implementation lives. `business` means a user-owned module, so the generated code imports it rather than inlining logic.

auth.description: PolicyExpr source. Parsed once, on the TypeScript side, into a JSON AST that the runtime interprets; the string form never reaches a runtime.

kind.description: `memory` is the fully supported default and is what every gated test uses; `pgvector` is declarable in Phase 1 but no gate requires a database, so a pgvector-backed app is never the only thing that can pass.

uri.$comment: The pattern *is* the requirement: it cannot express a literal DSN, so a committed credential is out of scope by construction - the same trick `model.apiKeyEnv` uses. The security gate re-checks the resolved value, because the IR can carry a uri the schema never saw.

dimensions.description: Vector width. It must agree with the embedding model's own width; the normalize gate compares the two.

knowledgeDataSource.description: Where a managed knowledge base reads documents from. The kind is the engine's own source: `s3` for Bedrock Knowledge Bases and `gcs` for Vertex AI RAG, because neither engine can read the other's bucket.

knowledgeBase.description: A managed knowledge base: the cloud owns ingestion, chunking, embedding, the vector store and the index, and the runtime only asks it for chunks. Declarable from spec v0.12. A retriever binds to one with `knowledgeBase`. The engine owns ingestion, so a deploy never starts it: a base whose corpus is empty fails the first retrieve with an error naming the missing job, and the emitted README names the command that starts one for this engine. It also owns the schema, so `refresh` is refused beside the binding and `aid migrate --check` reports a managed base as not applicable. The emitted module sets `prevent_destroy` on the base and on any vector store it creates, and `aid infra plan` warns when the saved plan would delete either -- a teardown is allowed, it just cannot be silent; a replacement is not a delete. `aid doctor` reports the engine and the environment name the runtime reads without contacting the cloud, so it cannot say whether ingestion has run: the first retrieve answers that.

engine.description: Which cloud's managed knowledge base this is. `aws-bedrock` is Bedrock Knowledge Bases; `vertex-rag` is the Vertex AI RAG Engine. Both are reachable only from their own cloud, which the infra emitter checks against `--cloud`.

chunking.description: How the managed engine splits documents. The engine performs the split, so this is configured on the knowledge base rather than performed by the runtime.

embedModel.description: Model alias that must declare `embeddings`, and whose provider must belong to the same cloud as `engine`. The knowledge base owns the vector store, so this replaces the store-width gate rather than being exempt from it.

filterable.description: Metadata keys the filter contract may use. Bedrock sources need metadata sidecar files for a filter to match anything, so this is what makes the emitter write the sidecar convention instead of a filter that silently matches nothing.

vectorStore.description: Where the engine keeps vectors. `provisioned` (the default) has the module create one; `existing` points at a store the operator already pays for and requires `arn`. The plan's default is not OpenSearch Serverless: its two-OCU floor is the most common way this feature becomes a surprise bill.

gateway.description: A managed MCP gateway: the cloud hosts the endpoint, the targets behind it are federated tools, and a runtime reaches it over MCP instead of bundling every tool. Declarable from spec v0.24. The gateway owns its invocation surface, so a target here is a tool the app does not run -- which is why nothing in this section is copied into the generated tool registry: `tools:` is unchanged and a gateway is reached through an MCP client, not through a second emitter.

description.description: What this gateway is for. Carried to the resource's `Description`, which the CloudFormation reference caps at 200 characters.

targets.description: The federated tool targets this gateway fronts. Every kind is one target under the gateway's `Mcp` configuration, so a single shape carries them all.

gatewayAuthorizer.description: How a caller proves it may invoke the gateway. `awsIam` signs with SigV4 and is what a runtime on the same account uses; `jwt` validates a bearer token against an OIDC discovery document and is what an outside caller uses. The CloudFormation resource also accepts `NONE` and `AUTHENTICATE_ONLY`, which are deliberately unreachable: a gateway that authenticates nobody is reachable by anyone who learns its URL, and one that only authenticates forwards every request to a target the platform then authorizes with the gateway's own role.

kind.description: SigV4 request signing with an IAM identity. Maps to `AuthorizerType: AWS_IAM`.
A JWT bearer token validated against OpenID Connect discovery. Maps to `AuthorizerType: CUSTOM_JWT`.

discoveryUrl.description: The OIDC discovery document the gateway reads to find the issuer's signing keys. The platform requires the `.well-known/openid-configuration` suffix, so the pattern refuses a bare issuer URL here rather than at apply time.

audience.description: Accepted `aud` values, at least one. A token minted for another audience is refused by the gateway rather than by the target.

gatewayTarget.description: One federated target behind a gateway. `kind` selects which of the two configurations below is required, and the other is refused rather than ignored: a target that carried both would describe two tools, and the CloudFormation resource accepts exactly one per target.

name.description: The target's name, used for the resource name and the tool prefix the gateway advertises.

kind.description: `openApiSchema` federates every operation in an OpenAPI document; `mcpServer` federates every tool an existing MCP server already exposes.

description.description: What this target fronts. Carried to the target resource's `Description`.

gatewayOpenApiSchema.description: An OpenAPI document the gateway reads to advertise one tool per operation. Either an object-store URI or the document itself, never both: the CloudFormation `ApiSchemaConfiguration` accepts `S3` or `InlinePayload`, and a target that named both would leave the platform choosing which one wins.

uri.description: `s3://` URI of the document. The pattern is the one the CloudFormation `S3Configuration.Uri` property documents, so an invalid URI is refused here rather than at apply time.

bucketOwnerAccountId.description: The 12-digit account that owns the bucket, when it is not the account deploying the gateway. Required for a cross-account bucket, refused otherwise by the platform.

inline.description: The document itself, for a schema too small or too changeable to publish to a bucket. Written verbatim into the target's `InlinePayload`.

gatewayMcpServer.description: An MCP server the gateway proxies: the app reaches one gateway URL and the platform reaches every tool the server behind it exposes. Nothing is copied here -- the server keeps owning its own tool list.

endpoint.description: The server's HTTPS MCP endpoint. The platform refuses a plaintext endpoint, so the pattern is enforced at build time rather than at apply time.

knowledgeBase.description: Bind this retriever to a managed knowledge base. It replaces `source`, `chunking`, `embedModel`, `store` and `index` -- declaring one of those beside it is ambiguous and refused rather than silently preferred.

kind.description: `file` indexes a local directory and is implemented at every version. `s3` loads an object-store corpus and `http` loads exactly one URL; both are implemented at spec 0.21. `db` and `mcp` are reserved by the design and rejected by a spec-local rule until the phase that ships their loaders, so a spec can be written against the final spelling without being silently ignored.

glob.description: A pattern selecting documents from a `file` or `s3` source, using `*`, `**`, `?` and literal text. For `s3`, the pattern matches object keys relative to the uri's prefix. An `http` source is one document and takes no `glob`, because a pattern describes a set.

strategy.description: `fixed`, `recursive` and `code` cut a document by size. `semantic` cuts where the cosine similarity between adjacent units dips, so a boundary follows the text rather than a character count; it is implemented at spec 0.22, and a spec-local rule rejects it below that version.

size.description: Target chunk size in characters. The cost gate turns it into tokens at a fixed characters-per-token ratio, so estimates compare.

embedModel.description: Model alias that must declare the `embeddings` capability; the referential gate enforces that.

hybrid.description: Blend the lexical and the vector ranking instead of ranking on the vector alone. Off by default, so a retrieval that needs no lexical half declares nothing.

topK.description: Candidates the retriever returns per query. This is the retriever's value; Phase 1 has no step-level override.

model.description: Model alias the reranker is bound to. Phase 1 ships a deterministic lexical reranker, so the alias is a `fake` or local model; a hosted reranker adapter is a later phase's seam.

filters.description: Expressions that narrow a query to the passages it may see, ANDed in order. The grammar is `<field> <operator> <value>` with operators `==`, `!=`, `^=`, `$=`, `*=`. `<field>` is a chunk metadata key, or the reserved `doc_id`/`uri`; a value containing spaces is quoted with single or double quotes. A field a chunk does not carry never matches, for every operator including `!=`, so a corpus cannot opt out of a selector by omitting the key. Requires spec 0.20.

mode.description: How a rebuild treats work already in the index. `full` re-embeds and upserts every chunk without deleting anything; `incremental` treats the documents it is given as the whole corpus, embeds only chunks whose content hash is not stored, and deletes the vectors of documents the corpus no longer contains.

schedule.description: Spec 0.23. A five-field cron (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week) read as UTC, at which the compiler emits a scheduler resource for this retriever: `aws_scheduler_schedule` submitting the AWS Batch job, or `google_cloud_scheduler_job` calling the Cloud Run job's `:run` endpoint. Each field is `*`, `*/n`, a number, `a-b`, `a-b/n`, or a comma list of those; six-field expressions, `@daily`-style macros and the `?`, `L`, `W` and `#` extensions are refused. The retriever also needs a `target: batch` deployment to trigger, and a retriever that binds a managed knowledge base refuses `refresh` entirely because the managed engine owns ingestion.

traits.description: Behavioural traits the generated retrieval path must honour. `citations` means retrieved items carry the source path and offsets a generated answer can cite.

target.description: Only pipelines are evaluable in Phase 0.

gate.description: How this eval's result is compared against the committed baseline. Never an equality check: sampling noise is expected, so the gate is a threshold on the regression relative to the baseline.

ci.description: When true this eval runs in the CI gate. At least one eval per HTTP-triggered pipeline should set it (an IR warning, not a schema rule).

maxRegression.description: Largest tolerated absolute drop in the metric's score versus the baseline.

samples.description: Runs per case. More samples shrink the sampling-uncertainty term the gate also requires before it fails.

minMean.description: Absolute floor: the eval fails whenever the mean score falls below this value, regardless of maxRegression. A 0/1 metric (such as `assert`) needs it, because the regression allowance can otherwise absorb a drop it must never absorb. Required to be 1 when an `assert` metric is present.

kind.description: Allowed in the spec but rejected by a spec-local rule when gate.ci is true: a judging model is neither deterministic nor available offline, so it can never be part of the CI gate.
Deterministic and offline: it compares the ranking against known-correct source paths, so unlike llm-judge it is allowed under gate.ci.

expectDocs.description: Source paths, spelled relative to the retriever's source uri, that the ranking must place inside the top k. A warning in the eval-coverage gate if a spec declares retrievers and no eval measures them.

kind.description: Deterministic and offline: a closed predicate evaluated against the prediction and the case, so unlike llm-judge it is allowed under gate.ci. Needs `gate.minMean: 1.0`, which a spec-local rule enforces.

expr.description: A PredicateExpr over `prediction`, `case.id` and `case.metadata.<name>`. Closed grammar: no eval, no regex.

message.description: The failure detail, verbatim. Required: it is the whole value of a failing assertion.

kind.description: Scores a prediction with a `score` decision: the rubric is declared once in `decisions` and the answer's position becomes the metric. Not deterministic, so a spec-local rule rejects it under gate.ci.

decision.description: The name of a `decisions` entry whose `type` is `score`. A moving alias is refused, because two runs of an eval would otherwise score two different models.

trigger.description: How the pipeline starts. `http` mounts a route; `manual` starts nothing on its own and exists so a `target: batch` deployment can run the pipeline once to completion. Exactly one of the two is declared.

manual.description: A pipeline with no inbound route. A `target: batch` deployment names it and runs it once per job.

context.description: Binding name holding retrieved items: a retrieve step's result. The generator passes the items to the prompt and returns the citation list alongside the model call.

tool.description: Explicitly invoked by the pipeline, never chosen by the model. That is what keeps Phase 0 control flow plain async while still exercising the tool, auth and tracing seams.

retrieve.description: One retrieval over a declared retriever, bound to `as` for a later generate step's `context`. Retrieval is an explicit pipeline step rather than something a step does implicitly, so what was searched and in what order stays visible in the spec.

query.description: Mustache-style text, checked for well-formedness like a prompt template. A placeholder naming a later step's binding is a build-time IR error, not a schema one.

rerank.description: Reorders a retrieval result with the reranker named by `model`. The runtime's reranker takes both a query and the items, so the step names both: `over` is the retrieval binding it reorders and `query` is what it ranks against. The design doc's single `input` field could not supply both, so it is not part of this shape.

over.description: Binding name holding the retrieval result to reorder: a retrieve step's or an earlier rerank step's `as`.

query.description: Mustache-style text the reranker scores against, checked for well-formedness like a prompt template.

model.description: Reranker alias matched by the runtime, not a `models[]` entry. Only the lexical reranker is implemented, so the name must contain 'lexical'.

guard.description: Runs one declared guardrail against one payload at one stage. A blocked payload stops the pipeline the same way an input-stage guardrail does on a generate step; a `flag` records a verdict and changes nothing, which is why a guard step binds no name.

text.description: Mustache-style text for the `input` and `output` stages; at the `retrieval` stage a single reference to a retrieval binding, whose passages are what the guardrail inspects.

agent.description: Runs a declared agent to completion and binds its answer. The step owns a fresh run of that agent, so it declares `text` (the user turn) rather than an `input` map; an agent that can pause, or that declares `memory`, is not a legal target.

text.description: Mustache-style text sent as the agent's user turn.

branch.description: Authorization branching. `when` is evaluated against the caller's Principal, so it answers "who is asking" and never "what did the last step produce" -- the grammar has no operand for a context value. Use `map`/`reduce` for data-driven control flow.

when.description: A policy expression over the authenticated caller. Parsed by the IR layer, which rejects an operand that is not a builtin call or a literal.

parallel.description: Runs each arm concurrently under the deployment's single concurrency cap. Results merge into one context, in branch order.

map.description: Applies one step to every item of a bound list, concurrently, and binds the ordered list of results.

over.description: Binding name holding the list to iterate.

reduce.description: Applies one prompt to every item of a bound list, concurrently, and binds the ordered list of results. Combining them into a single value stays explicit in a following `generate` step.

over.description: Binding name holding the list to iterate.

route.description: Data-driven control flow: asks a declared `choice` decision what the input is, then runs the arm its answer names. Every label the decision can return must reach an arm, so an answer never has an unhandled continuation; `default` covers the labels `on` leaves out. Unlike `branch`, whose `when` sees only the caller's Principal, `input` is a template, so routing may depend on what an earlier step produced.

decision.description: A declared decision of type `choice`. A `score` or `noul` answer names no arm, so neither is a legal router.

input.description: The text the decision classifies. A mustache template over earlier bindings, like a `retrieve` step's query.

on.description: The arm to run for each answer label. A key the decision never returns is refused, as is a decision whose label has no arm and no `default`.

default.description: The arm for a label `on` leaves out. Required when `on` is partial; refused when `on` already maps every label, because it could never run.

as.description: Binding name for the chosen label, so a later step can name the path it took.

stepList.description: An ordered list of steps: a pipeline body, or one arm of a composite.

binding.description: Name a step's result is bound to for later steps.

stepInput.description: Flat map of scalars. A string may be a single {{path}} reference or a template containing several; nested values are deliberately out of scope for Phase 0.

instructions.description: Prompt alias supplying the agent's instructions.

onBudgetExhausted.description: What a budget breach does. `fail` (the default) is a hard failure. `degrade` steps once to the first cheaper fallback alias; it requires maxCostBudget and a cheaper fallback, which the agents gate enforces at build time.

handoffs.description: Agents this one may transfer the conversation to; the receiving agent owns the rest of the turn.

delegates.description: Agents this one may delegate a sub-task to; control returns to this agent when the sub-task finishes.

engine.description: Who owns the loop. `native` is the AID agent runtime; `deepagents` delegates to the pinned framework, which requires an engineVersion.

when.description: Closed policy expression deciding when a human must approve.

provider.description: The decision vendor. Closed: `typesafe` is the only one the runtime serves.

model.description: A pinned Jev version such as `jev-1.14.0`. Moving aliases (`jev-latest`, `jev-preview`) are refused inside `evals`, where a score must be reproducible.

instructions.description: The question, in one sentence. Not a prompt template: Jev does not carry a conversation.

oneOf.description: `choice`: a label -> description map. Labels are the answers.
`score`: 2 to 10 ordered levels; position is the score.

onError.description: What a failed call means for a guardrail that names this decision. `block` (the default) keeps the gate closed when the vendor is unreachable; `allow` keeps an advisory check from stopping traffic. A `route` and an eval metric still fail the run, because neither has an arm or a score to fall back on.

guardrail.description: A check at one stage. A guardrail is either a policy check (`policies` + `action`) or a decision-backed check (`decision` + `onDecision`); it may declare both, and the policy check runs first.

stages.description: A decision runs at `input` only; the other stages see payloads a classifier question was not written for.

allOf.$comment: A managed guardrail (spec 0.11 for Bedrock, 0.14 for Model Armor) is evaluated by the cloud, so it names no local detector and no decision, and the managed API only sees prompt text.

stages.description: A managed guardrail API takes text and answers with text: there is no chunk payload and no tool arguments to send.

allOf.$comment: Declaring where a managed guardrail's policy lives is the statement that the guardrail is managed; the reverse direction would read as a comment.
The Model Armor counterpart of the `bedrock` rule above, from spec 0.15: a `modelArmor` block is the spec owning the template.

policies.description: Closed policy vocabulary; a name the guardrails engine does not implement is rejected at the spec layer, never passed through.

engine.description: Who evaluates the declaration. `builtin` (the default) is the runtime's offline detector layer; `bedrock` is a managed AWS Bedrock guardrail; `model-armor` (spec 0.14) is a Vertex AI Model Armor template in Google Cloud, owned by the spec from 0.15 when a `modelArmor` block is present. An engine is a location for the policy, not a policy itself, so a managed guardrail carries no `policies`.

bedrock.description: The managed policy a `bedrock`-engine guardrail owns, rendered into the deployment as an `aws_bedrock_guardrail`. Omit the block to point the app at a guardrail the operator already owns, through `BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_ID` and `BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION`. Account ids and ARNs are never spec inputs.

content.description: Content-filter strength per category; the same strength is applied to input and output. A category absent from the map is not filtered.

topics.description: Denied topics, name -> the definition the classifier is given. The definition is the policy: two specs that name the same topic but describe it differently are asking different questions.

words.description: Exact terms the managed word filter refuses.

pii.description: Personal-information entities the managed policy detects. `action: redact` anonymises them; `action: block` refuses the text instead.

modelArmor.description: The managed policy a `model-armor`-engine guardrail owns, rendered into the deployment as a `google_model_armor_template`. Omit the block to point the app at a template the operator already created, through `MODEL_ARMOR_TEMPLATE`. DLP inspect/deidentify templates and custom filter rules are references to resources this deployment does not create, so they stay operator inputs.

rai.description: Responsible-AI categories the template filters, category -> the lowest confidence it refuses. A category absent from the map is not filtered.

promptInjection.description: Refuse prompt-injection and jailbreak attempts at this confidence or above. Absent leaves the filter off.

maliciousUri.description: Refuse text that carries a malicious or phishing URL. `false` writes an explicit `DISABLED`, which differs from omission only in intent.

sensitiveData.description: Inspect text for sensitive data with the basic configuration. `false` writes an explicit `DISABLED`. A DLP inspect or deidentify template is an operator input, not a spec input.

decision.description: A `choice` decision to ask before the stage runs. Only the `input` stage may carry one, and the name must be declared under `decisions` (spec 0.7).

onDecision.description: What each answer label means. `allow` lets the run continue; the others record that action. Every label the decision declares must appear here, and no other label may (checked by the spec gate, which knows the criteria).

minConfidence.description: The lowest answer confidence this guardrail accepts. A less confident answer counts as a failed check and fails closed as a block. Defaults to 0.

redact.description: Field names the `redact` action removes. Required when `action: redact`, which the guardrails gate enforces.

tools.description: Tools this guardrail covers. Absent or empty means every tool that reaches the stage.

scope.description: `thread` is one conversation, `user` spans a user's threads, `global` is shared by every caller.

backend.description: A declared store id or `in-process`. The memory gate resolves it.

cloud.description: The cloud this deployment lands in. Spec 0.25. Before 0.25 the cloud was only a CLI flag (`aid infra --cloud`, defaulting to `aws`), which put a property of the customer's deployment in whoever's shell happened to run the apply. When the spec declares it, the spec wins and an agreeing `--cloud` is ignored, while a disagreeing one is refused with `cli/infra-cloud-conflict` rather than silently dropped. When the spec omits it, `--cloud` decides, and `aws` when that is absent too -- byte-identical to the behaviour before this key existed. Deployments that pin *different* clouds are refused separately, by `ir/cloud-conflict`, because one module set targets one cloud.

region.description: The region the deployment is placed in, and the residency pin. Spec 0.25. A deployment scalar rather than a project one, because one project may place `prod` and `dev` in different regions. Validated against the region set of the deployment's cloud, so a region that belongs to the other cloud is `ir/region-target` at validate time rather than a module that fails at apply time.

audit.description: Where this deployment's audit record lands. Spec 0.25. The sink names a service the customer already owns; AID emits the log group or sink, never its contents. `enterprise` requires one on every deployment.

image.description: Where the image is published. Spec 0.4, and only on a `target: container` deployment: another target builds no image to publish.

pipeline.description: The pipeline this job runs, by id. Spec 0.5, and only on a `target: batch` deployment: a run-to-completion job exists to run exactly one pipeline once, and a target that answers requests runs whichever pipeline its route names. The pipeline must declare `trigger.manual`.

runtime.description: The managed agent runtime the process runs on. Spec 0.13, and only on a `target: container` deployment: the platform schedules, isolates and addresses the process, so the compute module is replaced rather than paired with it. The spec must declare exactly one HTTP route, because the platform's invocation route carries one request shape. The app is unchanged: the generated contract wrapper mounts the same ASGI app and route handlers, so the cost ceiling, trace span, eval hook and refusals stay on the invocation path.

A managed agent runtime: a service that stops being a container the operator keeps warm and becomes an agent the platform schedules, isolates and addresses. `aws-agentcore` is Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, one microVM per session with up to 8 hours; `gcp-agent-platform` is the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI Agent Engine, still `google_vertex_ai_reasoning_engine` in Terraform), a managed per-session runtime. Both accept the image `target: container` already builds, which is what makes this a deployment destination rather than a second generation path. `memory.shortTerm` maps to AgentCore Memory on `aws-agentcore` and to a Vertex AI Memory Bank on `gcp-agent-platform`, where it is configured on the reasoning engine through `context_spec.memory_bank_config`. `session.ttlMinutes` defaults to 480, the AgentCore microVM ceiling; the Google platform accepts up to 20160 (14 days).

platform.description: The platform that runs the process. The platform's credentials are the deploy's credentials, so a platform and `--cloud` that disagree are refused instead of deployed unreachable.

memory.description: Managed short-term memory. On `aws-agentcore` it is AgentCore Memory; on `gcp-agent-platform` it is a Vertex AI Memory Bank on the reasoning engine. Short-term events are the session transcript; long-term memory is deliberately absent until the spec has a construct that names what is stored and who may read it.

shortTerm.description: Store the session transcript in managed memory: AgentCore Memory on `aws-agentcore`, a Vertex AI Memory Bank on `gcp-agent-platform`. The backend forgets an event after 30 days.

session.description: How long one session may live. Defaults to 480 minutes, the AgentCore microVM ceiling.

ttlMinutes.description: Session lifetime in minutes. AgentCore microVMs stop at 480; the Google platform accepts up to 20160 (14 days).

gateway.description: Name of a `gateways` entry this runtime reaches over MCP. Spec 0.24, `aws-agentcore` only: the gateway is an AgentCore resource and the Google platform has no counterpart. Presence does two things and nothing else: the emitted module exports the gateway URL into the runtime's environment and grants the runtime role `bedrock-agentcore:InvokeGateway` on exactly that gateway. The app keeps its own tool list -- a gateway adds tools it does not own, it does not replace one it does.

audit.description: The audit destination for a deployment: a service the customer already runs, named rather than configured here. Each sink belongs to one cloud, and a sink named for the other cloud is refused (`ir/audit-target`) instead of emitted as a resource the deploy cannot create.

sink.description: The log destination. `cloudwatch` and `s3` are AWS; `gcs` and `bigquery` are Google Cloud.

retentionDays.description: How long the record is kept, in days. Omitted means the sink's own default, which is the honest answer: AID does not invent a retention policy for an operator's log store, and no lifecycle rule is emitted at all rather than one guessed. When the document does name one, every sink honours it, each in its own provider's terms: a CloudWatch log group via `retention_in_days`, an S3 archive via a lifecycle expiration, a GCS bucket via a lifecycle rule, and a partitioned BigQuery dataset via a partition expiration. Two deployments naming the same sink with different retention are different destinations, and `ir/audit-conflict` refuses them.

image.description: Where the image for a `target: container` deployment is published. `ghcr.io` needs no credential: a generated release workflow pushes there with the `GITHUB_TOKEN` it already has. Every other registry declares the fields its login reads -- `docker.io` (spec 0.16) the *names* of two repository secrets, `aws.ecr` (spec 0.17) the account, region and role the workflow federates with, and `gcp.artifact-registry` (spec 0.18) the project, region and Workload Identity pair. No credential value is ever written into the spec.

registry.description: The registry to publish to. Each has its own credential path: `ghcr.io` uses the workflow token; `docker.io` uses the two secrets below; `aws.ecr` and `gcp.artifact-registry` exchange the run's OIDC identity for a short-lived cloud credential.

name.description: Repository path under the registry, without the host, e.g. `acme/support-copilot`. Lowercase, because a registry rejects the alternative. On `gcp.artifact-registry` the project is prefixed to it when the image reference is emitted.

usernameSecret.description: Repository secret holding the account name. Required on `docker.io`, refused elsewhere: a registry that logs in with the workflow token or a federated cloud identity has no stored account.

tokenSecret.description: Repository secret holding the access token. Required on `docker.io`, refused elsewhere, for the same reason.

accountId.description: The AWS account that owns the repository. Required on `aws.ecr`, refused elsewhere. The registry host is derived from it and `region`, so it is never written twice.

region.description: The region the registry lives in. Required on `aws.ecr` and `gcp.artifact-registry`, refused elsewhere: `us-east-1` for ECR, `us-central1` for Artifact Registry.

roleArn.description: The IAM role the release workflow assumes through GitHub's OIDC provider. Required on `aws.ecr`, refused elsewhere. A role ARN is an identifier, not a credential: nothing is assumed until the workflow exchanges its OIDC token for it.

project.description: The Google Cloud project that owns the repository. Required on `gcp.artifact-registry`, refused elsewhere; the emitted repository path is `<project>/<name>`.

workloadIdentityProvider.description: The Workload Identity Provider the release workflow federates with. Required on `gcp.artifact-registry`, refused elsewhere.

serviceAccount.description: The service account the federated identity impersonates. Required on `gcp.artifact-registry`, refused elsewhere.
